label: Whatever has the nine is INCOMPREHENSIBLE_2, from finite caused intellects
meaning: Let g have the nine; g is INFINITE_1 (one of the nine). Let x be an intellect whose being some other being causes. By the first premise x is not INFINITE_1; by the second, an intellect that is not INFINITE_1 does not comprehend the INFINITE_1 being g. Hence no caused intellect comprehends g, and g is INCOMPREHENSIBLE_2. Only the infinity conjunct of the nine is used. Conditional consequence; both premises stay open, and the conclusion is INCOMPREHENSIBLE_2, not INCOMPREHENSIBLE_1. Why two premises rather than the single weaker one the step needs (no caused intellect comprehends an INFINITE_1 being): the split separates two independently assessable claims with different warrants and different rivals (caused being is not unreceived being, q.7 a.2; finite power cannot know the infinite as much as it is knowable, q.12 a.7), so each can be derived or refuted on its own; the single weaker premise follows from the two.
